learning_outcomes.statement: Dispels the belief that every event handler receives an event, and inventories the tkinter.Event object -- which fields exist and which are meaningful for which event types.

This is an AI-only pass; it cannot issue APPROVED.

criteria.rationale: Factual correctness -- command= calls the function with no arguments; .bind(sequence, callback) calls it with exactly one argument, the Event; mixing them up is a common cause of TypeError. -- verified via code_execution: confirmed -- a 0-arg function works fine as command=, and the same function bound via .bind() produces 'TypeError: no_arg() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given' through Tkinter's exception reporter.; Event is one class for all event types, so event.x/event.y are meaningful for mouse events but not keyboard, and event.keysym/event.char for keyboard but not hover. -- verified via code_execution: confirmed -- a <Key> handler receives keysym='Return', char='\r'; an <Enter> handler receives widget='.!label', type='7' with no meaningful keysym. Matches the warning exactly.; event.widget is the widget the event relates to -- a UI source, not game state. -- verified vi
